label: no
controls_available: A visible irregular 6-by-9 chart with six band labels, three block labels, directional brackets, valid cells, and five missing cells; the chart and fleet manifest are informational rather than directly clickable controls.

Three full-mode SVG rotary selectors for Band, Block, and Count; the agent drags each knob to a labeled detent. Band values are the six seeded labels, Block values are A/B/C, and Count values are 1 through 9 plus *.
The FIRE button submits the currently selected band/block/count designation; * consumes one of the two sweep charges and covers a whole band/block run.
The END ATTEMPT button becomes CERTIFY FLEET after all vessels are sunk; certification and the post-failure CONTINUE control are administrative controls.
autonomous_processes: None in the puzzle mechanic: the generated chart, hidden fleet placement, and selector options remain fixed between agent actions.
Selector changes and Fire resolve synchronously in the pointer or click handler; hit, miss, sunk, shot, and sweep state changes occur only inside those handlers.
The 600-second allowance and shared clock are deadline/runtime machinery, not a task-state process; certification performs asynchronous result I/O only after an administrative action.
grouped_control_modes: D_fire: every fire_button shot across seeds, rounds, and attempts, parameterized by the currently selected band/block/count designation, including * sweeps.
D_rotary_drag: every full-mode rotary_drag on a Band, Block, or Count selector; it synchronously changes the next designation but does not itself fire.
END ATTEMPT/CERTIFY is administrative and is excluded from an outcome-affecting real-time witness.

clause_i.reason: For the efficiency-bearing terminal outcome, no policy using only its own action history can be optimal across different seeded chart topologies and different persistent hit/miss states: the best next designation can depend on the visible chart and evidence. A fixed enumeration can still eventually pass, but the grader explicitly gives fewer-shot completions a higher efficiency score, so that observation-free enumeration is not the optimal low-shot action in every such history.

clause_ii.reason: A single current screenshot is sufficient: it contains the chart topology, band/block/count direction labels, persistent hit/miss/sunk marks, fleet manifest, shot count, and remaining sweeps. Because shot evidence is rendered persistently, a bounded window of 0 ms with its one endpoint frame can support the adaptive next-designation policy; no older frame is required.

clause_iii.reason: With no new action, the visible chart and all outcome-affecting state remain unchanged for every positive delay within the task allowance. Waiting cannot make a rotary detent or Fire designation unavailable or less effective; any chart change follows Fire or administrative certification, not autonomous non-clock evolution. Thus for no valid D, Delta, and 0 < tau < Delta is there a strict Q loss caused by task-state evolution.

common_visible_process: None. Persistent chart evidence supports visual search, but there is no autonomous visible process whose evolution could both determine a delayed action and degrade that action opportunity.

pre_run.reason: There is no autonomous outcome phase to start: the outcome-affecting Fire actions are the phase, and the world does not advance on its own between them. The mathematical classification is already No because clause (iii) fails, so the pre-run threshold cannot change the label.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 5 is the 6-by-9 irregular, reverse-count, no-orientation, touching-vessel, five-hole profile with fleet lengths 4/3/3/2 and two sweeps; full mode uses rotary detent drags, and the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame.

Generation builds a seeded static chart and fleet, samples holes and block boundaries once, computes fixed cell designations, and exports the world and runtime fleet; no timer, motion, or autonomous update is generated.

The task describes an unknown fleet whose shots reveal a persistent evidence chart, routes completion through verifier.py, and explicitly notes that persistent evidence removes a temporal-memory requirement.

The shared browser shell loads the mechanic's JS and CSS and invokes its render function; an unknown external mechanic falls through to that loader, with no Coordinates-specific animation or update loop added by the shell.
Full mode renders three SVG rotary selectors and records synchronous rotary_drag selections after pointerdown/pointerup geometry checks.

The board renders the fixed chart and persistent marks; Fire synchronously resolves the current designation, updates seen/hits/sunk/shots/sweeps, and redraws, while render installs only event handlers and no timer or animation callback.
Certification posts the already-collected event tape and handles the server response after the administrative button action; it is not an autonomous task evolution.
The relevant CSS is static layout and styling for the chart, selectors, buttons, and verdict; it declares no animation or transition that changes task state.
The grader replays selector and Fire events synchronously, derives outcomes from the fixed world and fleet, and passes only when all vessels are sunk; efficiency is a separate fewer-shot score.
The task verifier loads the exported result and independent grader and returns the replay pass/fail result, with no clock or elapsed-time condition.

The ordinary-input solver uses rendered cell classes for persistent hit/miss/sunk feedback and computes straight-vessel candidates before choosing the next designation, supporting a normal screenshot-only adaptive search rather than continuous observation.

The shared clock advances registered timers and animation frames only while a run window is active; this mechanic registers none, and its configured zero-length observation window supplies no autonomous task progress.
Task setup injects the selected control condition into the generator and treats real_time as run identity while keeping state generation time-agnostic.
The shared verifier helper only copies and parses the exported result before the mechanic-specific replay; it introduces no task-state evolution.
